items.followUp: Define floriculture and state one way it can provide employment.

rubric.why: Award for identifying horticulture as the cultivation of garden plants.
rubric.description: Defines horticulture as the cultivation of garden plants, such as fruits, flowers or ornamental plants.
rubric.how: Look for cultivation or growing linked to garden plants, fruits, flowers or ornamental plants.

rubric.why: Award for explaining how the profession can be adopted.
rubric.description: States that horticulture can be adopted through relevant education or training, or by working in a related field.
rubric.how: Look for education, training, or work such as in a nursery, orchard or landscaping.

modelAnswer: Horticulture is the cultivation of garden plants, including fruits, flowers and ornamental plants.
A person can adopt this profession by getting education or training in horticulture and working in a nursery, orchard or landscaping.

items.followUp: Name one career related to horticulture and state the training that could help prepare for it.

rubric.why: Award for identifying Bu Ali Sina as a renowned physician.
rubric.description: States that Bu Ali Sina was a famous physician.
rubric.how: Look for physician, doctor or medical work.

rubric.why: Award for naming his major medical achievement.
rubric.description: Names his book Al-Qanun-fil-Tib (Canon of Medicine), which was used as a standard medical text for centuries.
rubric.how: Look for the title Al-Qanun-fil-Tib or Canon of Medicine.

modelAnswer: Bu Ali Sina was a famous physician and Muslim scientist.
He wrote Al-Qanun-fil-Tib (Canon of Medicine), which remained a standard medical book for centuries.

items.followUp: What does the branch of biology called microbiology study?

rubric.why: Award for correctly identifying the subject studied in botany.
rubric.description: Botany is the branch of biology that studies plants.
rubric.how: Look for plants linked to botany.

rubric.why: Award for correctly identifying the subject studied in zoology.
rubric.description: Zoology is the branch of biology that studies animals.
rubric.how: Look for animals linked to zoology.

modelAnswer: Botany is the branch of biology that deals with the study of plants.
Zoology is the branch of biology that deals with the study of animals.

items.followUp: State one biological problem that could be investigated using the biological method.

rubric.why: Award for describing the biological method as an organised procedure.
rubric.description: Defines the biological method as a systematic or stepwise procedure for solving biological problems.
rubric.how: Look for systematic or stepwise linked to solving or investigating a biological problem.

rubric.why: Award for stating its purpose or importance.
rubric.description: Explains that it is used to investigate or solve problems related to living organisms.
rubric.how: Look for solving or investigating a problem related to biology or living organisms.

modelAnswer: The biological method is a systematic procedure used to investigate and solve biological problems.
It is important because it helps us find answers to questions about living organisms and their processes.

rubric.why: Award for explaining that observations gather information about a problem.
rubric.description: Observations are information gathered about a problem by using the senses, often with the help of instruments.
rubric.how: Look for gathering information through the senses or observation.

rubric.why: Award for naming the two types of observations.

modelAnswer: Observations are information gathered about a biological problem by using our senses, sometimes with the help of instruments.
The two types of observations are qualitative and quantitative.

items.followUp: State two functions of the nucleus.

rubric.why: Award for stating the membrane's boundary or protective role.
rubric.description: The cell membrane surrounds the cell and separates or protects its contents from the outside environment.
rubric.how: Look for surrounds, separates, encloses or protects the cell or its contents.

rubric.why: Award for stating that the membrane regulates exchange.
rubric.description: The cell membrane selectively controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
rubric.how: Look for controls or regulates movement in and out, or selectively permeable.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane surrounds and protects the cell contents, separating them from the outside environment.
It selectively controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

items.followUp: Name the national tree and national flower of Pakistan.

rubric.why: Award for naming Pakistan's national animal.
rubric.description: The national animal of Pakistan is the markhor.

rubric.why: Award for naming Pakistan's national bird.
rubric.description: The national bird of Pakistan is the chukar partridge.

modelAnswer: The national animal of Pakistan is the markhor.
The national bird of Pakistan is the chukar partridge.

items.followUp: What is binary fission, and in which kind of organisms does it commonly occur?

rubric.why: Award for identifying the structural reason prokaryotes do not undergo mitosis.
rubric.description: Prokaryotes lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus, so they do not undergo division of a nucleus by mitosis.
rubric.how: Look for absence of a true nucleus or nuclear membrane, or the statement that mitosis is nuclear division.

rubric.why: Award for naming the actual mode of prokaryotic cell division.
rubric.description: States that prokaryotes divide by binary fission instead of mitosis.
rubric.how: Look for binary fission or binary division.

modelAnswer: Prokaryotes have no true, membrane-bound nucleus, and mitosis is the division of a nucleus.
Therefore, prokaryotes do not divide by mitosis; they divide by binary fission.
